summary: Backend parity testing for /api/community-feed vs /api/feed (friends). 10/10 pytest tests passed. Validated: community-feed items now include activity_id, user_id, is_liked, likes_count, comments_count, user_upvoted; like/unlike on an activity_id from community feed correctly toggles is_liked and updates likes_count; add/delete comment correctly updates comments_count; friends feed not regressed; community-photos/photo-of-the-week and landmarks/{id}/community-photos still work.

minor.issue: Items from user-created-visit source without an activity doc will have activity_id=None — like/comment buttons in UI must be hidden or the backend should auto-create activities for these visits. Not a regression but a UX gap.

action_items: Consider backfilling / auto-creating an activity document for user_created_visits so the Community tab like+comment buttons work for custom visits too (currently activity_id may be None for those items → frontend should fall back gracefully).
Duplicate POST like returns 400 'Already liked' — frontend must treat 400 as an optimistic-UI-ok state (not an error toast) when is_liked was already true in a stale feed.
critical_code_review_comments: community.py: After aggregating items, the final `items.sort(..., reverse=True)` + `items[:limit]` is applied AFTER landmark and custom visits are independently queried with limit N each, so the merged list is pre-truncated per-source. With limit=10 you can get up to 20 items joined, then sliced to 10. Slightly wasteful but correct.

community.py: `activity_ids_v += [...]` builds list across two sources before the single batch-fetch of likes/is_liked — good (no N+1). is_liked post-processing correctly walks items and matches by activity_id.

community.py `likes_count` returned from activities collection is overwritten by the authoritative count from the likes collection (lines 227-233) — good, keeps parity with /api/feed which also computes from likes collection.

feed.py POST /activities/{id}/comment increments activities.comments_count via $inc; community-feed reads from activities.comments_count first then is not overwritten afterwards (unlike likes_count). If the counter drifts (e.g., comment deleted while activity doc missed the decrement for any reason), community-feed will show stale counts. Consider computing comments_count from `comments` collection in community-feed for true parity with the likes approach.
community.py returns is_liked=False in initial dict then overwrites in second pass — minor readability; could set inline.
seed_data_creation: Tests create/delete one TEST_parity_comment per run and toggle a like; all state restored after each test.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend parity verified. Frontend React Native testing was explicitly skipped per request. For next iteration, if verifying frontend, note web preview shows Expo onboarding so UI automation is unreliable — test on mobile simulator. Test account `activity_d9811bf4c810` is heavily used by these tests; counts are restored but be aware of concurrent test interference.
